overturned: chapter 12's runnable core, H_w = min(shoal(H_0,d), gamma*d), cannot produce the reform its own bar section is about -- the cap has no memory of the energy the break removed, so the wave never un-breaks. A dissipation model with memory (Dally, Dean & Dalrymple 1985) is required, and --bug cap-not-dissipation shows what the chapter's line costs.

chapter 27's 'wavelength-scale filtered depth' is wrong inside a morphodynamic loop: at L/10 = 13 m it HIDES an 11 m bar from the wave that should break on it, disabling the feedback that limits the bar's growth. Right for a renderer's break mask, wrong where depth is a state variable.

the Longuet-Higgins 5*pi/16 longshore coefficient was DERIVED rather than cited, by a suite row failing at 23 per cent: pi/4 comes from the depth gradient of S_yx and the missing quarter is alongshore refraction, since sin(theta) ~ sqrt(d) in shallow water.

Soulsby (1997) does not reduce to Stokes in the fine limit -- its asymptotic coefficient is 1.049/(2*10.36) against Stokes' 1/18, a fixed 8.9 per cent shortfall. Recorded as a property of the published fit.

the Iribarren breaker-class thresholds (0.5/3.3 vs 0.4/2.0) are BOTH attributed to Battjes 1974 and differ because one is in deep-water and the other in local quantities -- the same trap family as E_0/4 vs E_b/2. beach.breaker_class refuses to carry one table.

gap: Section B's SECOND breaking line is STILL not achieved and is still an OPEN row, but the cause is now closed-form rather than guessed. The reform is a DISTANCE condition: the wave needs 1.71 e-foldings of the Dally decay between crest and trough and gets 0.86. Equivalently, at the loop's own 15 m back slope it needs 1.11 m of relief and has 0.71 m; at its own relief it needs a 30 m back slope. The trough it digs is exactly ONE decay length d/K behind the crest (L*K/d = 0.95 0.99 1.09 1.19 1.24 across H_0 = 1.0-3.0 m), because the undertow that scours it is driven by a dissipation that decays over d/K -- so the morphology inherits the wave model's own length scale and a one-bar breakpoint model is short by a factor of about two by construction. Named plainly: what is missing is a SECOND bar, and a second bar needs the alongshore circulation and inner-surf feedback that chapter 12 puts out of scope with the 2DH model. A missing mechanism, not a missing tolerance.

result: The four candidate causes were separated. (1) RELIEF is live but was misdescribed: reform is a joint condition on relief AND cross-shore distance and distance binds -- the loop's own 0.90 m of relief reforms when spread over 30 m instead of 15, giving surf zones at 360-388 m and 453-500 m with 65 m of calm between. (2) DECAY RATE is the same axis (the e-folding count is K*L/d); reform needs K ~ 0.35-0.40 against the flux-form standard 0.15. (3) NO MEMORY is dead: the transform marches the flux and carries gamma_b/gamma_s hysteresis, proved by --bug no-hysteresis and by the probe row. (4) FORCING HISTORY is dead and reverses: storm/calm cycling, +-0.5 and +-1.0 m semidiurnal tide, and 3/5/8-quantile Rayleigh height distributions ALL lower the relief; steady monochromatic forcing is the most favourable case this model has. (5) THE GRID, added on a parallel builder's question, is also dead: refining space and time together (dt at 0.6 of the slope term's diffusion bound dx^2/(2*6.7e-4)) the trough minimum runs 0.4574 / 0.4607 / 0.4629 / 0.4625 at dx = 2.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 m -- converged and moving AWAY from 0.40, while the relief converges downward 0.62 / 0.52 / 0.48 / 0.44 m. Every mechanism tried trades trough width against relief, which is why the 14 per cent gap is robust rather than marginal.

closed_forms.saturated_surf_ratio: DERIVED THIS WAVE: Gamma_eq = gamma_s/sqrt(1 + (5/2)(dd/dx)/K), the fixed point of the Dally march with the shallow-water flux substituted. A broken wave on a SHOALING bed decays to a ratio strictly above gamma_s, 0.477 on this scene's inner slope (measured 0.4748). Verified against the marched transform on plane slopes 1:150-1:60 to 3 per cent, and corroborated by Raubenheimer, Guza & Elgar (1996), who measured saturated H/h at 0.2-1.0 positively correlated with local bed slope -- a field paper neither side was written from.
closed_forms.saturation_slope_limit: DERIVED THIS WAVE: tan(beta)_crit = 2K/5 = 0.060 (1:16.7), the slope above which the closed form's denominator vanishes and no saturated surf zone exists -- the shoaling gain outruns the breaking loss and the wave surges. Lands within a factor of 1.5 of Wright & Short's reflective/intermediate boundary, so the breaker-type classifier and the wave-decay model are not independent statements.
closed_forms.reform_criterion: DERIVED THIS WAVE: G(d) = G_eq + (G_c - G_eq)(d/d_c)^-a with a = K/m + 5/2, G = (H/d)^2, m = dd/dx down the back of the bar. The exponent carries K/m, so the decay is paid for in TRAVEL DISTANCE and not in depth gained. Checked against the marched transform bisected on relief across L = 10-75 m; the closed form runs a systematic 0.15-0.25 m optimistic because it assumes a straight back slope and shallow water.
closed_forms.breaker_index: unchanged and now measured in ONE depth field: d_bar/(H_b/gamma) = 0.973 at dx = 1 m and 0.981 / 0.973 / 0.982 / 0.992 across dx = 2.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 m.

overturned: WAVE 1's OWN d_bar/(H_b/gamma) = 0.893 AND ITS FALSIFIABLE TREND ARE WITHDRAWN. The comparison straddled two depth fields -- H_b and d_b come out of the transform, which reads the wavelength-filtered depth, while cr['d'] is the raw bed, and the 1.5 m filter lifts an 11 m crest by 0.19 m. In one field the ratio is 0.973. Refining the grid, the raw form climbs 0.852 / 0.893 / 0.940 / 0.971 while the same-field form does not move; the sea-state trend is the same curve along a different axis, because a bigger bar is a broader bar and a fixed filter takes proportionally less off it. A parallel builder reached the same conclusion independently from the discretisation. Chapter 12's d_bar ~ H_b/gamma is met to 1-3 per cent and is NOT asymptotic.

gamma_s = 0.40 is not the H/d a surf zone relaxes to. It is the FLAT-BED limit of a slope-dependent family, Gamma_eq = gamma_s/sqrt(1 + (5/2)(dd/dx)/K). A chapter naming gamma = 0.78 as the breaking index should not let a reader infer a second constant a broken wave decays to.

Chapter 12's 'the profile breathes on a storm/calm cycle' does not build a wider bar in 1-D -- it builds a LOWER one. Storm/calm cycling, tidal cycling and a Rayleigh height distribution were all measured and all reduce the relief, because a moving break point smears the flux convergence into a terrace. The breathing is real as a statement about bar MIGRATION; read as a mechanism for bar RELIEF it is backwards.

break_lines() was being read as 'the breaking lines' and it is the ONSET test. H/d >= gamma marks where a wave starts breaking and says nothing about where one stops, so on this profile it returns a single 1 m interval and empty space over a 140 m band of white water. surf_zone_spans() reads the transform's own hysteretic state and is what section B's criterion is about.

Wave 1's 5*pi/16 was filed under 'overturned' as if chapter 12 carried a wrong coefficient. The chapter carries no coefficient at all -- it writes V_long proportional to ... and stops -- so it is an ADDITION to the chapter, not a correction. Settled by a parallel builder this wave; recorded so nobody inherits a phantom disagreement.

Wave 1's suspicion that its own transform might collapse to the memoryless min(shoal, gamma*d) form somewhere is refuted. --bug no-hysteresis removes only the off-switch and the probe row catches it. The chapter's core lacks the memory; this file's does not; the reform still fails, for an unrelated reason.

result: THE SURF LINES FOLLOW THE CURVE, and it is measured rather than eyeballed. The embayment is an OUTPUT of chapter 12's coastal loop run in plan with a spatially varying hardness: corr(shoreline, hardness) = -0.95, amplitude 55 m on 189 m of mean retreat, and the same loop with hardness set to 1 leaves 0.45 m of amplitude against 45.6 m with it -- the chapter's 'uniform rock gives a straight cliff and nothing else', run as an experiment. The wave transform is a 2-D energy-flux march with Snell nowhere in it; it contains Snell as its degenerate case (k_y invariant to 0 on an alongshore-uniform bed) and reproduces the 1-D transform to 4.4e-16 m at normal incidence. Four measurements of the criterion, each with a refraction-frozen control: crest-to-contour angle at breaking 7.2 deg against 13.4 frozen; crest azimuth regressed on contour azimuth, slope 0.366 (R2 0.67) against 9e-17 frozen and a closed-form bound of 0.513; outer surf line correlated with the shoreline at r = 0.939 over 89 stations; the bar sits 123 +- 8.2 m seaward of its OWN local shoreline while that shoreline swings 55 m. The shore normal itself swings 56 deg across the bay.

closed_forms.refraction_2d: THE FIRST REFRACTION TEST IN THIS PROJECT THAT DOES NOT PASS BY CONSTRUCTION. On a plane beach whose contours run at 10/20/30 deg to the grid, the march reproduces Snell about the ROTATED normal to 0.186/0.310/0.277 deg, and to 0.000 at zero rotation where it degenerates into wave 1's identity again -- and the row was FIRST WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT FLATTERS, reading 0.030 at 30 deg because its window was pinned to the grid centre, where a rotated ramp barely reaches. Independently: an RK2 ray tracer with different equations agrees with the march over the bay's curved contours to 0.043 rad, against 1.6e-3 rad on a straight coast.
closed_forms.crest_turning: DERIVED THIS WAVE: d(theta)/d(beta) = 1 - c(d)/c(d_ref), the rate at which a crest turns onto a contour whose normal lies at azimuth beta. A crest is parallel to its contour only in the limit c -> 0, so 'crests parallel to the depth contours' is a bound and not an assertion. Bound 0.513 at d = 1.7 m with d_ref the 8 m shelf; measured regression slope 0.366.
closed_forms.breaker_index: d_bar/(H_b/gamma) = 0.935 +- 0.028 across 89 independent cross-shore profiles that the coastal loop shaped differently from one another, both terms in ONE depth field. The mixed-field form gives 0.563 -- the trap is worth 0.37 of the ratio in 2-D against 0.08 in 1-D, because the filter is 1.5 cells and these cells are four metres.
closed_forms.obliquity: DERIVED THIS WAVE: chapter 12's 1-D march applies the Dally rate per unit CROSS-SHORE distance and a divergence applies it per unit RAY distance, ds = dx/cos(theta), so the two forms differ by cos(theta) in the exponent. Measured 4.4e-16 m / 2.6 mm / 8.0 mm at theta_0 = 0/20/40 deg. Small only because refraction turns the wave to 6.6 deg before it breaks.

overturned: CHAPTER 12'S coastalStep DOES NOT RETREAT A COAST ON A HEIGHTFIELD. `band` reads the cell's own elevation, so once the notch has cut the toe below the band and the thermal step is holding the face at repose above it, no intact rock is in reach: 16 m of retreat in 1500 steps and 0.0 m in the 500 after that. Widening notchHeight restarts the retreat and destroys the bench, so the chapter's own platform diagnostic and its retreat loop are in conflict as written. The missing term is UNDERCUTTING, which a heightfield cannot hold (chapter 11's representation warning, which 12 already invokes for arches); its heightfield expression is that waves attack the first land cell above the waterline. With it, both halves of the diagnostic work.

ITS DEPOSITION STEP LOSES THE ROCK IT ERODES. beach = (1 - exposure)*nearShore is identically zero over open water, where the fetch sweep saturates, and LARGEST on the dry plateau, where the sweep returns zero because no fetch reaches a cell behind a cliff. Measured: 116154 m^3 lost out of a closed domain in one version, and the shoreline stalled at 0.4 m of retreat in another. Three corrections and none is a coefficient -- the band is water, the material stays in the row it came from (moving it alongshore IS longshore drift), and the fill is capacity-limited at the datum with the excess exported and reported. 90 per cent of the debris leaves, which is what a real cliff does with it.

NOTHING IN THAT SECTION LIMITS THE PLATFORM'S WIDTH: 235 m of bench and still widening at 1600 steps, because nothing attenuates the wave crossing it. The feedback is the chapter's own breaking index -- the wave reaching a cell is min(H_0, gamma_b*d) and the work goes as H^2 -- so a cliff behind a wide shallow bench is attacked by a small wave. Added at NO new constant.

THE DALLY DECAY CARRIES AN OBLIQUITY AND THE CHAPTER'S 1-D FORM IS THE OTHER ONE. dF/dx = -(K/d)(F - F_s) with F = E c_g cos(theta) applies the rate per unit cross-shore distance; the divergence form a plan view needs applies it per unit ray distance. Same statement only at normal incidence. Reported and deliberately NOT patched into the 1-D file, which is what waves 1 and 2 measured with.

WAVE 1'S PLAN FIGURE IS WITHDRAWN AS A DEPICTION OF THIS SCENE. It inserted one cross-shore profile at every alongshore station and stamped chapter 12's ripSystem rhythm through it, and said so in its own caption. Wave 3 removes both: the cross-shore profile now differs at every station because the coastal loop gave each one a different shoreface (crest depth 0.62 to 1.71 m, sd 0.23 m, on ONE offshore sea state), and no alongshore rhythm is stamped at all -- with the honest consequence that there are NO RIP CHANNELS, because the 2DH circulation that carves them is still out of scope.

THE TWO-FIELD ERROR CLASS BIT TWICE MORE, BOTH TIMES IN TEST CODE, AND IT COSTS MORE IN 2-D. The ray-tracer against-the-march row disagreed by 0.270 rad -- 15 degrees of apparent refraction error -- until both were read from one depth field, when it fell to 0.043. The crest-depth ratio reads 0.935 in one field and 0.563 in two. And a THIRD guard belongs beside the first: a masked statistic must state the sign convention its mask enforces -- the crest-to-contour angle came back at 34 deg mean with a 173 deg p95 until the mask excluded cells behind the bar crest, where the depth gradient reverses and the shoreward normal points out to sea.

WAVE 2 FIXED THE ROWS THAT RAISED AND LEFT THE HARNESS ABLE TO BE LIED TO. The suite is now a list of SECTIONS called through a guard, with an ERROR status that counts against the exit code; an exception costs its own section and nothing after it. It earned its keep on the first run: four sections raised at once and the run still reported 58 passing rows and the two real FAILs underneath them.
